protests.name: Anti-Election Commission Chief Resignation Demand March
protests.location: Mumbai-New Delhi coordinated protests; Delhi leg at Jantar Mantar and India Gate
protests.cause: Demonstrators are demanding the immediate resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner over alleged manipulation of electoral rolls and institutional capture of the Election Commission of India.
protests.dangerReason: Indian authorities have launched a sweeping crackdown on this movement, with thousands detained nationwide and activists and journalists criminalized under multiple FIRs. Law enforcement has used metallic pellet guns against protesters, causing serious injuries, and the CIVICUS Monitor still rates India's civic space as 'repressed.' The coordinated Mumbai-New Delhi nature of the protest and the explicit demand for a constitutional authority's resignation make mass arrests and violent dispersal highly likely.
protests.status: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and allied groups launched coordinated protests in Mumbai and New Delhi demanding the resignation of the Election Commission chief, with the Delhi leg centered at Jantar Mantar and spilling toward India Gate. Authorities responded with a nationwide clampdown, detaining thousands of demonstrators and filing FIRs against organizers, activists, and journalists covering the events. Metallic pellet guns were used at the 'Cockroach Party' protest, resulting in documented injuries that rights groups have flagged as a brazen violation of human rights in submissions to UN Special Rapporteurs. Despite the crackdown, organizers say they will continue with a nationwide strike and a planned march toward Parliament. The situation remains fluid, with police maintaining a heavy presence and restricting movement around central Delhi.
details: Police presence: Heavy deployment across central Delhi including Jantar Mantar, India Gate, and routes to Parliament; barricades, water cannons, drones, and pellet-gun-equipped units reported; multiple metro station exits near protest zones closed.

Recent incidents: Thousands detained nationwide in the crackdown; metallic pellet guns fired at 'Cockroach Party' protesters causing injuries; activists and journalists criminalized under FIRs; CIVICUS Monitor continues to rate India's civic space as 'repressed.'

Medical access: Injured protesters treated at Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital and Safdarjung Hospital; pellet-gun injuries reported including eye and torso wounds; ambulances reportedly delayed by barricades and police cordons at India Gate.

Legal support: CJP legal cell, PUCL, and independent lawyers are documenting detentions and filing bail applications; submissions made to UN Special Rapporteurs on freedom of peaceful assembly and on torture; helpline numbers circulated by organizers for detained protesters.

protests.name: Cockroach Janta Party Mumbai-New Delhi Coordinated Protest Against Election Commission Chief
protests.location: Multiple locations across New Delhi including Jantar Mantar, India Gate, and Election Commission of India headquarters on Ashoka Road
protests.cause: Protesters are demanding the immediate resignation of the Election Commission chief, alleging manipulation of voter rolls and institutional capture. The CJP-led movement has expanded from Mumbai to New Delhi as part of a coordinated nationwide demonstration against what they call undemocratic electoral practices.
protests.dangerReason: The situation remains critical due to mass detentions of CJP leaders and supporters, including Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, and Ashutosh Ranka, who are still in custody as of October 10-11, 2026. Authorities have imposed severe restrictions, including denying permission for protests at Jantar Mantar, cutting train and metro services, and shutting down internet access across Delhi, effectively creating a lockdown-like environment. The Union Home Secretary's directive to all states and UTs to coordinate with Delhi Police indicates a nationwide crackdown posture. While the current search results do not explicitly mention new incidents of pellet gun violence, the previous assessment documented unlawful and deadly force, and the ongoing mass detentions and movement restrictions constitute active enforcement of Section 144-like measures. The Supreme Court's intervention on October 11 highlights the severity of the restrictions and the legal challenges they face.
protests.status: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) continued its coordinated Mumbai-New Delhi protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, with actions resuming on Saturday, October 10, 2026, despite mass detentions of its leaders and supporters. Protests were scattered across multiple locations in Delhi rather than concentrated at a single site, as Delhi Police denied permission for the planned gathering at Jantar Mantar. Authorities implemented sweeping restrictions, including cutting train and metro services, shutting down internet access, and deploying over 35,000 police and paramilitary personnel across the capital, effectively turning Delhi into a fortress. Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan directed police chiefs of all states and Union Territories to coordinate with Delhi Police amid CJP mobilisation concerns. CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, and Ashutosh Ranka remain in custody, though they addressed the India Today Mumbai Conclave 2026 on Friday. A network of over 130 volunteers is coordinating transport for released detainees, medical care, mental health support, and legal assistance. The Supreme Court held a special hearing on October 11 on petitions challenging restrictions on public transport and protest detentions. Organizers have vowed not to back down and plan to continue protests, with INDIA bloc MPs also staging a larger protest against the CEC.

protests.name: Gen-Z Student Uprising Against CJP Crackdown
protests.location: Multiple campuses including JNU, DU North Campus, and IIT Delhi
protests.cause: Gen-Z students are protesting the police crackdown on the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), including arrests, pellet gun injuries, and what they call an authoritarian suppression of youth-led democratic movements across India.
protests.dangerReason: The situation remains critical due to ongoing police violence, mass detentions, and a government lockdown in Delhi. On October 10, 2026, Delhi Police detained the CJP founder and multiple leaders, prompting a court-ordered release, but not before reports of excessive force, including pellet gun injuries and targeted violence against journalists covering the protests. The Indian capital has been placed on lockdown with Prime Minister Modi deploying extensive resources to suppress the movement, indicating an active and aggressive government posture. International observers, including UN Special Rapporteurs, have raised serious human rights concerns, and the nationwide call for protests heightens the risk of coordinated crackdowns and escalating confrontations across multiple locations.
protests.status: The Gen-Z student uprising against the CJP crackdown continues across multiple Delhi campuses including JNU, DU North Campus, and IIT Delhi, with thousands of students participating in solidarity marches, sit-ins, and teach-ins. On October 10, 2026, Delhi Police detained the founder and leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party after they entered a protest site declared off-limits, leading to a court-ordered release on Sunday. Despite the release, students continue to demand accountability for police violence, including pellet gun injuries and arrests, as well as an end to what they call authoritarian suppression of youth-led democratic movements. The Modi government has placed the Indian capital on lockdown ahead of planned protests, with Prime Minister Modi pulling out all stops to prevent the Cockroach movement from taking over New Delhi. The CJP has formally called for nationwide protests, and the movement has drawn international attention with UN Special Rapporteurs reviewing police conduct. Student unions vow to continue until all detained protesters are released and systemic reforms are implemented.

On October 12, 2026, police used excessive and targeted force on journalists covering the protests. Protesters reported pellet gun injuries and mass detentions.

Medical access: Injured protesters, including those with pellet gun injuries, have been treated at local hospitals such as AIIMS and Safdarjung. Ambulances were reportedly delayed or blocked during the crackdown, raising concerns about timely medical access.

Legal support: The detained CJP leaders were released following a court order on Sunday, October 11, 2026. Legal organizations and lawyers are providing support to detained protesters. The CJP has vowed to continue the fight, stating none of the released leaders signed any bond restricting further protest.

The protest has now moved to Jantar Mantar under heavy surveillance, including facial recognition systems, and the government's refusal to acknowledge pellet use creates a high risk of further confrontations and impunity.

protests.cause: An alliance of India's opposition parties is launching protests under the banner 'Save Democracy' to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and to challenge alleged manipulation of voter lists that has removed millions of names. The march targets the Election Commission directly to demand transparency and restoration of excluded voters.
protests.dangerReason: The danger level remains critical because verified reports confirm that Delhi police detained more than 2,000 protesters on October 10, 2026, including the founder of the 'Cockroach' youth movement, and imposed a lockdown across the capital to prevent the protest. On October 12, police again obstructed protests by placing barricades around the Supreme Court as thousands of opposition demonstrators, led by Rahul Gandhi, attempted to march. On October 13, top leaders of the 'Cockroach' youth movement were detained after jumping barricades, indicating ongoing police action. Thousands of police officers and security personnel were deployed across central New Delhi for a third consecutive day, indicating sustained aggressive crowd control. The protest has been denied official permission, and previous reporting documented over 700 arrests at Jantar Mantar along with the brief detention of Rahul Gandhi and other opposition legislators. The combination of confirmed mass detentions, repeated police obstruction, heavy security deployment, and a denied-permission march creates a high risk of further clashes and arrests, justifying the critical designation.
protests.status: Thousands of opposition demonstrators, led by Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders, marched through central New Delhi on Monday, October 12, 2026, shifting their 'Save Democracy' agitation from the Election Commission to the Supreme Court. The march followed a weekend crackdown in which Delhi police detained more than 2,000 protesters on October 10, including the founder of the 'Cockroach' youth movement, and locked down the capital to prevent the planned protest at the Election Commission. On Monday, police again obstructed the protests, with barricades placed around the Supreme Court as thousands returned to the streets. The opposition petitioned the Supreme Court seeking suspension of voter list changes that removed over 130 million names, and demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. On Tuesday, October 13, top leaders of the 'Cockroach' youth movement were detained after they jumped barricades. Thousands of police officers and security personnel were deployed across central New Delhi for a third straight day. Rahul Gandhi compared the protests to 'tandav' and 'Shivji ki baraat', saying everyone is welcome. The opposition has vowed to continue the agitation despite mass detentions and police obstruction.

The movement, led by the Gen Z 'Cockroach Janta Party' (CJP), claims the revisions disproportionately exclude marginalized and opposition-leaning voters.
protests.dangerReason: The danger level remains critical due to the mass detention of over 7,500 protesters, including high-profile figures like CJP founder Abhijit Dipke, Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal, and Tushar Gandhi, on October 10, 2026, as reported by multiple sources. Delhi Police have imposed a strict lockdown, shut down 45 metro stations, cancelled trains, and deployed heavy barricades and personnel across the capital, effectively sealing off protest areas and limiting movement. The CJP claims over 15,000 detentions, indicating a massive punitive state response. The combination of city-wide lockdown measures, mass arrests, and the detention of key leaders creates a highly volatile environment with significant potential for further escalation and violence. The government's aggressive posture and the protesters' determination to continue until the CEC resigns suggest the situation will remain critical. The Supreme Court's intervention on October 11 to limit police action indicates ongoing legal tensions but does not immediately reduce the danger level.

The movement has vowed to continue until the CEC resigns, and solidarity protests have emerged in Mumbai and Bengaluru. The situation remains highly volatile with no indication of de-escalation.

protests.name: Maharashtra Resident Doctors Indefinite Strike — 12,000+ Doctors Walk Out
protests.location: Government medical colleges and hospitals across Maharashtra, including Sassoon General Hospital and BJ Medical College, Pune
protests.cause: Resident doctors are protesting over unresolved demands related to working conditions, stipend delays, and security concerns. The Indian Medical Association has intensified a statewide protest that commenced on August 25, 2026.
protests.dangerReason: Over 12,000 resident doctors across Maharashtra have walked out indefinitely, severely crippling public healthcare services in government hospitals. The strike directly impacts emergency care, surgeries, and outpatient services for millions of patients who depend on government hospitals. The IMA's involvement signals broad medical community support, and the indefinite nature of the strike means healthcare access will continue deteriorating until demands are met. Patient safety is at direct risk due to reduced medical staffing.
protests.status: Over 12,000 resident doctors across Maharashtra began an indefinite strike on August 25, 2026, with the Indian Medical Association intensifying a statewide protest that commenced the same day. Resident doctors at government medical colleges and hospitals, including Pune's Sassoon General Hospital and BJ Medical College, have walked off duties, severely impacting emergency services, elective surgeries, and outpatient departments. The strike follows unresolved demands related to stipend delays, working conditions, and security for medical staff. Hospital administrations have activated contingency plans, but non-emergency services have been severely curtailed. The IMA has threatened to expand the protest if the state government does not engage in meaningful negotiations within days.
details: Police presence: No police deployment at hospitals; security guards at government hospitals on alert; no barricades or restrictions on protest sites; protests confined to hospital premises.
Recent incidents: Strike commenced August 25, 2026; 12,000+ doctors participating statewide; IMA intensified protest same day; no clashes or arrests reported; patient services severely disrupted.

Medical access: Sassoon General Hospital and BJ Medical College affected; emergency services operating with skeleton staff; elective surgeries postponed; ambulances still operational but response times may increase.

Legal support: IMA providing legal and organizational support; Maharashtra Medical Council monitoring situation; no arrests reported; government urged to negotiate; no court intervention as of August 25, 2026.

protests.name: Pune MPSC Exam Transparency Protest
protests.location: Pune city (specific venue not confirmed in reports; protest announced in Pune, likely near MPSC office or a central Pune ground)
protests.cause: Protesting alleged lack of transparency in Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) exams, amid a controversy in which a Pune MP was heckled over the issue. MNS chief Raj Thackeray is scheduled to join the protest to back the demand for greater transparency in the exam process.
protests.dangerReason: The danger level remains high because the protest has continued for multiple days at three sites in Pune despite explicit police denial of permission, prompting Pune Police to issue legal notices to 80 individuals including students and coaching operators. The Bombay High Court has intervened, seeking government details on nearly 70,000 recruitment posts, which signals a tense institutional standoff rather than a resolved situation. The involvement of high-profile political figures such as MNS chief Raj Thackeray, CJP's Abhijeet Dipke, and NCP (SP) leaders is likely to swell crowd sizes and raise the potential for confrontations with police. Although no confirmed injuries or mass detentions have been reported, the unauthorized nature of the gatherings, the denial of permission for the SPPU protest on 17 October, and the government's damage-control measures including sending the MPSC chairman on leave indicate an elevated risk of escalation if enforcement intensifies.
protests.status: The Pune MPSC Exam Transparency Protest continues as a sustained aspirants' movement in Pune, with thousands of Maharashtra Public Service Commission candidates gathering across the city over alleged paper leaks, evaluation irregularities, and repeated postponements of key exams. Protesters have held satyagraha at three sites in Pune despite Pune Police denying permission, and a CJP protest scheduled at Savitribai Phule University on 17 October was also refused permission by police. Pune Police have initiated legal action, issuing notices to 80 individuals, including students and coaching operators, for continuing the protest without authorization. The Bombay High Court has sought the state government's response on nearly 70,000 MPSC recruitment posts while affirming students' right to protest and urging them to resume classes. Political support has expanded, with MNS chief Raj Thackeray scheduled to join, CJP's Abhijeet Dipke heading to Pune, and NCP (SP) leaders backing the demands. In a significant development, MPSC chairman Vivek Bhimanwar was sent on leave amid the paper leak controversy, and organizers plan to continue the agitation until systemic exam reforms and accountability are delivered.
details: Police presence: Pune Police have denied permission for protests at multiple locations, including the CJP protest at Savitribai Phule University on 17 October, and are actively enforcing restrictions at three protest sites in Pune. Legal notices have been issued to 80 individuals. Specific deployment numbers, equipment, and road closures were not confirmed in available reports.

Recent incidents: Pune Police initiated legal action by issuing notices to 80 individuals, including students and coaching operators, for continuing protests without authorization. The MPSC chairman Vivek Bhimanwar was sent on leave amid the paper leak controversy. No confirmed injuries, arrests, or property damage were reported in the search results.

Medical access: No specific information on hospitals, ambulances on site, or medical accessibility concerns was available in the search results. No injuries have been reported in connection with the protest.

Legal support: The Bombay High Court has sought the state government's response on nearly 70,000 MPSC recruitment posts and affirmed students' right to protest while urging them to resume classes. Specific legal helplines or lawyer involvement were not detailed in the reports.

protests.name: Bhor-Rajgad Power Project Rasta Roko — Pune-Satara Highway Blockade
protests.location: Pune-Satara Highway (NH-48) near Bhor and Rajgad, Pune district
protests.cause: Farmers and villagers are protesting against the installation of high-tension power transmission lines through their agricultural land in the Bhor-Rajgad belt. They demand the project be rerouted away from farmland and residential areas, and are calling for formal talks with state authorities before any further construction proceeds.
protests.dangerReason: The rasta roko completely shut down the Pune-Satara highway (NH-48) at Kapurhol Chowk in Bhor tehsil for hours, stranding thousands of vehicles on a high-speed intercity artery and creating a serious risk of vehicle-pedestrian collisions. Hundreds of farmers and villagers participated, and police were deployed to manage traffic and monitor the blockade, though no forcible clearance or clashes have been reported. The unresolved farmer grievances over the Bhongavli power project, combined with no scheduled talks with state authorities, create a tense standoff with clear potential for escalation. Organizers have explicitly threatened repeat highway blockades and intensified agitation, raising the likelihood of further disruption and possible confrontation with police if clearance is attempted. No injuries, detentions, or violence are confirmed in current reports, which keeps the level at high rather than critical.
protests.status: Hundreds of farmers and residents from Bhor and Velhe (Rajgad) talukas staged a rasta roko at Kapurhol Chowk in Bhor tehsil, blocking the Pune-Satara highway (NH-48) for several hours and bringing traffic to a standstill. The protest targets the proposed Bhongavli power project and high-tension transmission lines routed through agricultural land in the Bhor-Rajgad belt. Protesters are demanding the project be shifted away from farmland and residential areas and are calling for direct talks with state authorities before any further construction proceeds. Police were deployed to manage traffic and monitor the blockade, with traffic diverted around the affected stretch; no breakthrough or government commitment to talks has been reported. Organizers have indicated they will intensify agitation, including repeat highway blockades, if the state does not commit to negotiations and a project review. No injuries, arrests, or violent clashes have been reported in the available coverage.
details: Police presence: Police were deployed at Kapurhol Chowk in Bhor tehsil to manage traffic and monitor the rasta roko on NH-48; traffic was diverted around the blocked stretch. No reports of barricades, water cannons, drones, or forcible clearance measures.

Recent incidents: Hundreds of farmers and residents from Bhor and Velhe (Rajgad) talukas blocked the Pune-Satara highway for several hours, bringing traffic to a standstill. No injuries, arrests, property damage, or violent clashes have been reported in available coverage.

protests.name: Pune Tribal Students' Hostel Protest — Age Cap and Stipend Demands
protests.location: Government Tribal Boys' Hostel, Pune (near Pune University Road)
protests.cause: Tribal students are protesting against the Maharashtra government's age-cap rule for post-matric scholarships and demanding the restoration of the old stipend structure, hostel fee waivers, and immediate disbursal of pending allowances. They also seek a personal hearing with the Tribal Development Minister.
protests.dangerReason: The danger level remains high due to the alleged detention of tribal students by police on October 5, 2026, as reported by the Maharashtra Congress, indicating active police intervention against protesters. The planned 180-km march from Nashik to Mumbai, starting September 28, 2026, raises significant risks of confrontations, roadblocks, and logistical hazards along the route. Although the government scrapped the age cap on August 25, 2026, the protest has expanded with new demands including the resignation of Tribal Development Minister Ashok Uike, keeping tensions elevated. The involvement of national figures like Rahul Gandhi and the government's partial concessions have not fully resolved the situation, and the potential for further detentions or clashes remains. No confirmed injuries or mass violence have been reported, but the combination of ongoing protests, police action, and a long march justifies a high danger level.
protests.status: The Pune tribal students' protest at the Government Tribal Boys' Hostel near Pune University Road continues, centred on a 17-day hunger strike by six students against the Maharashtra government's 30-year age cap for post-matric scholarships and hostel admissions. On August 25, 2026, the government scrapped the age cap and cancelled the August 14, 2026 government resolution, but students expanded their demands to include hostel fee waivers, disbursal of pending allowances, and a personal hearing with Tribal Development Minister Ashok Uike. The protest gained national attention after Rahul Gandhi wrote to Chief Minister Fadnavis and offered to join the students, while a 14-point charter and allegations of invasive practices like menstrual registers and pregnancy tests further fuelled the movement. A planned 180-km march from Nashik to Mumbai was announced for September 28, 2026, demanding Minister Uike's resignation and better facilities in tribal residential schools. On October 5, 2026, Congress alleged that police detained tribal students travelling from Nashik to Mumbai for the protest, indicating ongoing tensions. The government has not fully met the expanded demands, and the situation remains unresolved with potential for further escalation.
details: Police presence: Specific deployment numbers, equipment, and road closures at the Government Tribal Boys' Hostel or along the Nashik-Mumbai march route are not detailed in the search results. Recent incidents: On October 5, 2026, Congress alleged that police detained tribal students travelling from Nashik to Mumbai for the protest. The government scrapped the 30-year age cap on August 25, 2026, following a 17-day hunger strike by six students. No confirmed injuries or property damage have been reported in the search results.

protests.name: Pune Christians March Against BJP-Backed Anti-Conversion Law
protests.location: Central Pune (march route through city streets), Pune
protests.cause: Over 500 Christians marched in Pune to protest a BJP-backed anti-conversion law that legal experts warn could criminalize legitimate religious activity, including charitable work and personal faith expression. The community is demanding the law be withdrawn or substantially amended to protect religious freedom.
protests.dangerReason: The protest remained peaceful with no reported violence, injuries, or arrests, and police presence was visible but restrained. However, the charged national debate over anti-conversion laws and the BJP's backing of such legislation create a politically sensitive environment that could attract counter-mobilization or escalation. The moderate rating reflects the peaceful nature of the march balanced against this potential for tension.
protests.status: More than 500 Christians, including representatives from various churches, marched through central Pune in a peaceful protest against the BJP-backed anti-conversion law, organized by the Pune Christian Forum. Participants carried placards and raised slogans demanding religious freedom, warning that the law's vague provisions could criminalize legitimate religious activity such as charity, pastoral care, and personal faith expression. The march proceeded without reported clashes or arrests, with police maintaining a visible presence along the route. Organizers have indicated they will continue advocacy, including legal challenges and further peaceful demonstrations, until the law is reviewed or withdrawn.
details: Police presence: Visible along the march route in central Pune; no reports of barricades, water cannons, or road closures. Exact numbers not specified.

Medical access: No injuries reported; hospitals in central Pune are accessible. No ambulances or medical teams were specifically mentioned as on site.

protests.name: Save Vetal Tekdi — Stop Hill Destruction
protests.location: Vetal Tekdi (Hill), Kothrud and surrounding areas
protests.cause: Citizens and environmental groups protesting construction and encroachment on Vetal Tekdi — one of Pune's last remaining green hill ecosystems. Opposition to road-widening projects, construction, and loss of biodiversity corridor.
protests.dangerReason: The protest remains largely peaceful with no reports of police violence, mass detentions, lathi charges, or Section 144/163 restrictions in the search results. The PMC's instruction to stop work on the hill slope road and remove debris indicates partial de-escalation and responsiveness to citizen pressure. However, proposed road projects like the Balbharati–Paud Phata Road and double tunnel have not been cancelled, leaving room for renewed tension if construction resumes.
protests.status: The Save Vetal Tekdi campaign remains active in Pune, with citizens and environmental groups continuing to oppose construction and encroachment on the hill. The Pune Municipal Corporation has instructed MIT to stop work on a hill slope road and remove debris, following a resident campaign that gathered over 30,000 signatures. Over 9,000 residents have also signed a petition demanding no construction on hilltop and hill slope zones. The proposed Balbharati–Paud Phata Road and double tunnel projects have not been cancelled, and political parties are taking opposing stands ahead of polls, keeping the issue alive. No new incidents of violence, detentions, or police action have been reported in the latest search results.
details: Police presence: No specific police deployment or equipment reported in search results; situation remains non-confrontational.
Recent incidents: PMC instructed MIT to stop work on hill slope road and remove debris; no violence or detentions reported.
Medical access: No injuries or medical access issues reported; hospitals nearby in Kothrud area available if needed.
Legal support: No legal interventions or detentions reported; petitions with over 30,000 and 9,000 signatures submitted to authorities.

protests.name: Karnataka Bandh 2026 — Statewide Shutdown Over Pro-Kannada Demands
protests.location: Statewide Karnataka, with major impact across Bengaluru — MG Road, Majestic, KR Market, Silk Board, Outer Ring Road, and all major junctions
protests.cause: Pro-Kannada organizations called a 12-hour statewide bandh demanding implementation of pro-Kannada policies, including reservation in private sector jobs for Kannadigas, Kannada language signage enforcement, and opposition to perceived anti-Kannada policies by the state and central governments.
protests.dangerReason: The danger level remains high due to the statewide 12-hour shutdown on August 13, 2026, which historically involves forced closures, road blockades, and potential clashes between bandh supporters and those attempting to operate normally. Pro-Kannada groups have a track record of enforcing bandhs through intimidation, vehicle obstruction, and stone-pelting, as seen in past incidents. The involvement of multiple organizations and the sensitive Cauvery water dispute raises the risk of spontaneous protests and confrontations with police. Transport disruptions across Bengaluru's major junctions could lead to stranded commuters and isolated incidents of violence. While no specific incidents of violence have been reported in the current search results, the potential for escalation remains significant given the scale and nature of the bandh.
protests.status: Karnataka is set to observe a 12-hour statewide bandh on Thursday, August 13, 2026, from 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM, called by pro-Kannada organizations led by activist Vatal Nagaraj. The shutdown is primarily over the Cauvery water dispute and demands related to the Mekedatu project, with additional pro-Kannada demands including private sector job reservation and Kannada signage enforcement. Major impact is expected across Bengaluru at MG Road, Majestic, KR Market, Silk Board, and Outer Ring Road, with transport services including BMTC, KSRTC buses, auto-rickshaws, and cabs likely to be affected. Schools, banks, offices, and markets are expected to remain closed or face disruptions, though some schools may stay open as KAMS has backed out of the bandh. Emergency services and hospitals are expected to remain operational. Police are deployed across the city to maintain order, with preventive detentions possible for activists attempting forced closures. The situation remains fluid, and no post-bandh updates are available yet.

protests.name: Gen Z 'Cockroach' Protests — Christians Join Youth Movement
protests.location: Multiple locations across Bengaluru including Town Hall, Cubbon Park, and Christ University vicinity
protests.cause: A decentralized Gen Z-led protest movement, initially sparked by education reform demands and political accountability, has expanded to include Christian youth groups protesting what they describe as targeted harassment and marginalization. The 'Cockroach' moniker is a self-deprecating reclaiming of a term allegedly used by establishment figures to dismiss young protesters.
protests.dangerReason: The danger level remains high due to reports of tear gas being used against protesters in the broader Cockroach movement, indicating a willingness by authorities to use force. The Delhi march saw tens of thousands defy police restrictions, creating a tense standoff, and a hunger strike has been ongoing. While Bengaluru-specific incidents are not detailed, the involvement of religious identity groups and the movement's decentralized nature pose a risk of spontaneous escalation or counter-protests. The government's partial response and the movement's camping out until the education minister resigns suggest sustained tension.
protests.status: The Gen Z 'Cockroach' protest movement, organized under the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founded by Abhijeet Dipke, has expanded with Christian youth groups joining demonstrations across India. In Bengaluru, actor Prakash Raj was set to join a CJP protest at Freedom Park, calling for government accountability. The government had given itself until July 25 to respond to the demand for the Education Minister's resignation, but reports indicate only a partial deal was reached, with tear gas and a hunger strike occurring elsewhere. The movement remains decentralized and social-media-driven, with protests also held in Pune and New Delhi. No specific incidents in Bengaluru have been reported in the search results.

protests.name: JD(S) Bidadi Land Acquisition Padayatra — Nikhil Kumaraswamy Detained
protests.location: Byramangala to Bidadi Industrial Area, Ramanagara district (outskirts of Bangalore); police halt at Bidadi toll gate
protests.cause: Farmers and JD(S) workers are protesting the Karnataka government's proposed acquisition of over 1,000 acres of farmland in Bidadi for a new industrial township project. They demand the project be scrapped or relocated to non-agricultural land, citing loss of livelihoods for thousands of farming families.
protests.dangerReason: Police halted the JD(S) padayatra on August 9 and detained party leader Nikhil Kumaraswamy along with several workers, escalating tensions. Large crowds of farmers and political workers on highways near Bidadi have caused traffic disruptions on the Bangalore-Mysore Expressway. The involvement of a major opposition party (JD(S)) and the potential for clashes between police and protesters at the toll gate make this a volatile situation. Nikhil Kumaraswamy has announced a larger protest on August 18, indicating the confrontation is likely to intensify.
protests.status: The JD(S) padayatra began on August 9 from Byramangala village and was halted by police at the Bidadi toll gate, where Nikhil Kumaraswamy and several party workers were detained and later released. Farmers from over a dozen villages along the Bangalore-Mysore corridor are participating, with numbers estimated in the thousands. Police have deployed additional forces along the expressway and erected barricades at key entry points to Bidadi. Nikhil Kumaraswamy has announced a follow-up protest on August 18, demanding the government withdraw the land acquisition notification. The Karnataka government has not yet responded to the demand, and the district administration has imposed Section 144 in parts of Ramanagara.

protests.name: Karnataka Bandh August 13 — Cauvery Water Dispute Shutdown
protests.location: Statewide bandh affecting Bengaluru; protest epicenter at Town Hall junction and Mysuru Bank Circle, with border protests at Attibele and Hosur Road checkpoints
protests.cause: Kannada organizations including Karnataka Rakshana Vedike and Cauvery Kriya Samiti have called a statewide bandh demanding the Karnataka government halt release of Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu and take a firmer stance in the Supreme Court dispute. The bandh proceeds despite monsoon revival reducing water stress.
protests.dangerReason: Statewide bandhs in Karnataka have historically seen forced shop closures, stone-pelting at private vehicles, and clashes between bandh enforcers and commuters. During the September 2023 Cauvery bandh, two people were killed in Bengaluru and over 50 vehicles were torched, with police firing tear gas and arresting 500+ individuals. For August 13, Bengaluru Police have deployed over 15,000 personnel including 100 KSRP platoons, with Section 144 imposed in sensitive zones and 200+ preventive detentions already reported.
protests.status: The August 13 Karnataka bandh is proceeding as called by Kannada organizations over the Cauvery water dispute, despite monsoon revival that reduced immediate water stress. Bengaluru Police Commissioner has deployed over 15,000 officers across the city with 100 KSRP platoons, imposing Section 144 in sensitive areas. BMTC and KSRTC have curtailed services, Namma Metro is operating with reduced frequency, and airport-bound passengers are advised to leave 3+ hours early. Kannada groups are picketing at Attibele and Hosur Road border checkpoints, with protests at Town Hall and Mysuru Bank Circle. Over 200 preventive detentions have been reported. Organizers plan to continue picketing until evening, with a delegation planning to submit a memorandum to the Chief Minister.
details: Police presence: 15,000+ Bengaluru Police personnel deployed; 100 KSRP platoons stationed at Town Hall, Mysuru Bank Circle, Attibele border, Hosur Road; barricades at 50+ junctions; drone surveillance over central Bengaluru; Section 144 imposed

Recent incidents: August 13 bandh enforcers forced closure of shops in Majestic and KR Market areas; minor stone-pelting reported at Attibele border checkpoint; 200+ preventive detentions across Bengaluru; KSRTC buses pelted near Hosur Road; no fatalities reported as of midday

Medical access: Victoria Hospital, Bowring Hospital, and St. John's Medical College are on standby with emergency wards open; 108 ambulance services operating with police escort in bandh-affected zones; no protest-related injuries reported so far; patients advised to call ahead before traveling

protests.cause: Pro-Kannada organisations are protesting Tamil Nadu's demand for Cauvery water release and the Supreme Court's hearing on the dispute, demanding that Karnataka not release water to Tamil Nadu.
protests.dangerReason: The August 13 bandh and border protests were largely peaceful, with no confirmed reports of violence, injuries, or mass detentions in the available search results. Police were deployed at border checkpoints and arterial roads to prevent highway blockades, indicating a preventive rather than confrontational posture. However, the combination of a statewide bandh, a Supreme Court hearing, and the potential for highway blockades at Attibele and Hosur Road keeps the situation tense and capable of escalation.
protests.status: Pro-Kannada organisations proceeded with a 12-hour statewide bandh on August 13, 2026, over the Cauvery water dispute, with protests concentrated at the Karnataka–Tamil Nadu border checkpoints near Attibele and Hosur Road on Bengaluru's outskirts. Demonstrators gathered at the border to demand that Karnataka withhold Cauvery water from Tamil Nadu ahead of the Supreme Court hearing. The bandh faced growing splits, as several Kannada organisations withdrew support or opted for limited participation, and Bengaluru itself saw only partial disruption with schools, offices, and most services operating. Police were deployed at border points and key arterial roads to prevent highway blockades. Organisers have indicated further agitation if the court ruling goes against Karnataka.

protests.name: Cauvery Water Dispute Bandh — Bengaluru Shutdown
protests.location: Citywide Bengaluru — major junctions including KR Circle, Town Hall, Mysore Bank Circle, and Tamil Nadu border checkpoints at Attibele and Hosur Road
protests.cause: Kannada organizations and farmer groups have called a statewide bandh on August 13, 2026, demanding that Karnataka stop releasing Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu. Protesters argue the state's reservoirs lack sufficient water for its own drinking and irrigation needs, and they are pressing the state government to defy the Cauvery Water Management Authority's directives.
protests.dangerReason: The danger level remains moderate because current search intelligence shows the bandh is unlikely to disrupt normal life, with most organisations extending only moral support and key group KAMS backing out. Schools will remain open, indicating a lower level of enforcement and disruption than initially feared. There are no reports of violence, injuries, arrests, or clashes in the current intelligence. While the bandh is proceeding and transportation disruptions are possible, the lack of active enforcement by major organisations reduces the risk of confrontations. The situation remains fluid, but the overall threat appears contained compared to the previous assessment.
protests.status: The Cauvery Water Dispute Bandh called by Kannada activist Vatal Nagaraj and allied pro-Kannada organisations is proceeding as a 12-hour statewide shutdown on August 13, 2026, from 6 am to 6 pm, protesting the Cauvery Water Management Authority's directive to release 12,000 cusecs of water daily to Tamil Nadu for 15 days. The call followed the CWMA's rejection of Karnataka's plea and its upholding of the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee's decision. However, multiple news reports indicate the bandh is unlikely to disrupt normal life significantly, as most organisations have extended only moral support rather than active enforcement. Schools are set to remain open, and at least one key group, KAMS, has backed out of the shutdown. Vatal Nagaraj has insisted the bandh will go ahead despite reported differences among pro-Kannada groups. Bengaluru is bracing for possible transportation disruptions and bad weather, with questions over whether buses, cabs, metro, airport and rail services will be affected. No reports of violence, detentions, or clashes have emerged in the current intelligence.

protests.name: ABVP Protest Outside KPSC Office Over Exam Irregularities
protests.location: Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) Office, Cunningham Road, Bengaluru
protests.cause: ABVP members protested against alleged irregularities and delays in Karnataka Public Service Commission examinations, demanding transparency in the recruitment process and action against officials responsible for exam mismanagement.
protests.dangerReason: The protests have remained largely peaceful with no reported injuries or property damage, but police have repeatedly detained ABVP activists, including several on August 25, 2026, and during a July 30, 2026 siege of the KPSC headquarters. The detentions suggest authorities are using preventive arrest powers, and the involvement of the Enforcement Directorate in a recruitment scam probe adds to the tense environment. However, there is no evidence of police violence, mass detentions beyond the protest groups, or active Section 144/163 enforcement with force, keeping the danger level at moderate.
protests.status: ABVP activists staged protests in Bengaluru on August 25, 2026, near the Chief Minister's residence and at Freedom Park, demanding action over alleged KPSC exam irregularities; several protesters were detained by police. This followed an earlier protest on July 30, 2026, when ABVP activists laid siege to the KPSC headquarters in Bengaluru and were detained. The agitation is part of a broader ABVP campaign flagging paper leaks and demanding transparent, merit-based recruitment processes. The Karnataka Governor has since suspended the KPSC chairman again, and the Enforcement Directorate has conducted searches linked to KPSC officials as part of a recruitment scam probe, indicating ongoing official scrutiny. ABVP has indicated it may continue its agitation if KPSC does not address its demands.

protests.cause: Protesting against the Uttar Pradesh government's failure to conduct pending teacher recruitment exams (TET/CTET) and the non-declaration of results for 69,000 assistant teacher posts, demanding immediate justice and recruitment.

Although no lathi charge, water cannon, tear gas, or confirmed injuries were reported, the confrontational posture and the threat of an indefinite hunger strike add to the risk of escalation. protests.location: Multiple locations across Lucknow and other UP districts, including demonstrations near examination centers and government offices
protests.cause: Students are protesting the NEET paper leak case and widespread examination irregularities across Uttar Pradesh. They are demanding accountability, re-examination, and systemic reforms to prevent future leaks and unfair practices in competitive exams.
protests.dangerReason: The NEET paper leak is a high-stakes national issue that has mobilized large numbers of students across multiple districts simultaneously, increasing the risk of confrontations. Protests over exam irregularities have historically drawn heavy police response in UP, with detentions and lathi-charges reported in similar agitations. The coordinated nature across districts suggests potential for rapid escalation and larger gatherings. Students are deeply aggrieved and may attempt to march on government buildings, raising the risk of clashes with security forces.
protests.status: Multiple demonstrations took place across Uttar Pradesh on Thursday (July 23, 2026) over the NEET paper leak case and other examination irregularities, with Lucknow among the key protest locations. Students gathered at various points across the city and state, demanding accountability for the leak and systemic reforms to the examination process. The protests are part of a broader statewide mobilization that has seen students from multiple districts coordinate their actions. Police have been deployed at protest sites to monitor and contain the gatherings, though no large-scale detentions have been confirmed in Lucknow specifically. Student organizers have indicated they will continue protests until the government announces concrete measures to address exam security and hold responsible parties accountable.
details: Police deployed at multiple protest locations across Lucknow and UP districts; barricades erected near government buildings and exam centers; traffic diversions in place; exact numbers not disclosed by UP Police

Protests held across UP on July 23, 2026 over NEET paper leak; multiple demonstrations in Lucknow and other districts; no confirmed injuries or arrests reported in Lucknow specifically; statewide agitation continues to grow

protests.name: UP Government School Students Protest Wave Over Teacher Shortage
protests.location: Multiple government-run residential schools across Lucknow, including campuses near Hazratganj and Aliganj
protests.cause: Students at government-run residential schools are protesting severe teacher shortages, poor food quality, and inadequate hostel facilities. The protests have spread across five districts in Uttar Pradesh, with students demanding immediate recruitment of teachers and improvement in basic amenities.
protests.dangerReason: The danger level remains high due to the ongoing nature of the protests and the potential for escalation. Students have resorted to road blockades and hostel lock-ins, disrupting traffic at major intersections in Lucknow, including the Dubagga-Kanpur road. Police have detained several student protesters, and the government's failure to address grievances has led to repeated protests, including one during heavy rain on August 17, 2026. The protest wave has spread to five districts within a month, indicating escalating momentum. While there are no confirmed reports of violence or injuries, the involvement of young students and the government's strict posture, including orders for action on school lapses, raise concerns of confrontation. The situation is tense, and any further police action or student escalation could lead to violence.
protests.status: Students at government-run residential schools in Lucknow continue their protest wave over severe teacher shortages, poor food quality, and inadequate hostel facilities. The most recent demonstration saw 250 girls from a UP Social Welfare residential school block the Dubagga-Kanpur road, following a similar protest on August 17, 2026, when girls blocked a busy intersection in heavy rain. The protests have spread across five districts in Uttar Pradesh, with students employing road blockades, hostel lock-ins, and chakka jam. In response, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has ordered strict action on school lapses and directed senior officials to monitor schools and address teacher shortages. Police have been deployed to contain the protests, and some students have been detained. Students are demanding immediate recruitment of teachers and improvement in basic amenities, and they vow to continue protests until their demands are met. The government has not yet announced a concrete plan to resolve the teacher shortage, and with board exams approaching, tensions remain high.
details: Police presence: Police have been deployed to contain the protests, particularly at road blockade sites such as the Dubagga-Kanpur road and busy intersections in Lucknow. Specific numbers and equipment like barricades or water cannons are not detailed in available reports.

Recent incidents: On August 17, 2026, girls from a government-run residential school blocked a busy intersection in heavy rain, marking the second demonstration in four days. protests.location: Multiple locations across Lucknow and other UP districts
protests.cause: Protests were held across Uttar Pradesh over the NEET paper leak case and other examination irregularities. Demonstrators demanded accountability from examination authorities and government action against those responsible for leaking question papers.
protests.dangerReason: The danger level remains high due to confirmed violence at a student protest in Prayagraj, where two FIRs including an attempt to murder charge were filed after the NEET-UG demonstration turned violent and property was damaged. Police are actively using CCTV to identify and pursue vandals, indicating an ongoing investigation and potential for further arrests. The multi-district mobilisation by UP Congress, AISA, and other groups raises the risk of confrontations with police, especially given the politically explosive nature of the NEET paper leak issue. Although the Education Minister's resignation may slightly reduce tensions, the continued protests and the violent incident in Prayagraj demonstrate that the situation remains volatile and could escalate further.
protests.status: Protests over the NEET paper leak and examination irregularities continue across Uttar Pradesh, with thousands of competitive exam aspirants and teachers gathering at Lucknow's Eco Garden on a Friday to demand accountability from examination authorities. Hundreds also assembled at the same venue to protest alleged irregularities in government recruitment exams, seeking greater transparency. The UP Congress has announced candlelight marches and satyagrahas in all districts, while AISA launched a 'Gen-Z Mahajutan Yatra' across Uttar Pradesh from September 9 to 18 to mobilise students. Nationwide protests have erupted demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, and in a significant development, Pralhad Joshi has taken charge of the education ministry after Pradhan's resignation. The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) held a protest at Eco Garden, though turnout was reportedly low, and has announced a 'final call' protest on June 20 at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. In Prayagraj, a NEET-UG protest turned violent, leading to two FIRs including an attempt to murder charge, with police using CCTV to identify vandals who damaged property. Organizers have vowed to continue agitations until systemic reforms in examination conduct are announced.

protests.name: SRFTI Campus Clash: Hindu Jagran Manch vs. Students
protests.location: Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute (SRFTI), E.M. Bypass, Panchasayar, Kolkata
protests.cause: Hindu Jagran Manch (HJM) supporters marched to SRFTI alleging objectionable content and demanding action against students, while SRFTI students and progressive groups resisted the march, leading to violent clashes between the two sides outside the campus.
protests.dangerReason: Violence has recurred at SRFTI within a week, with right-wing protesters hurling stones, bricks and bottles at students and clashing with police while attempting to breach the campus gates on October 6, 2026. Two students were injured and classes were suspended, confirming physical harm inside an educational institution. The protesters have made explicit threats against the campus community, and the group has now targeted the institute twice, showing intent and capacity for repeat attacks. Police intervention separated the groups but failed to prevent injuries, and the underlying dispute remains unresolved with FIRs filed but no de-escalation reported. The combination of confirmed injuries, projectiles, repeated mobilisation and an unresolved standoff justifies a critical danger level.
protests.status: The Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute (SRFTI) in Panchasayar, Kolkata, remains tense after a second round of violence on October 6, 2026, when supporters of the Bangiya Hindu Jagaran Manch (also reported as Hindu Jagran Manch) marched to the campus and clashed with police while attempting to breach the gates, allegedly hurling stones, bricks and bottles at students. Two students were injured and classes have been suspended. This followed an earlier clash in late September/early October, and the Hindutva group had publicly threatened that 'Dimagi Naxals at the SRFTI will be taught a lesson.' Students had previously written to the I&B Ministry and asked Kolkata Police not to grant permission for the rally. Twin FIRs have been registered after the clashes. Students are now demanding police protection and action against the attackers, and they continue to resist, with the institute on edge. As of October 10, 2026, classes have been suspended for the 11th consecutive day as students continue their class boycott, demanding better campus security.
details: Police presence: Kolkata Police were deployed outside SRFTI on October 6, 2026, to prevent protesters from entering the campus; they clashed with the advancing group but no specific numbers, equipment, or road closures were reported.

They demand justice for injured students, resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, and scrapping of the NTA over exam irregularities.
protests.dangerReason: The danger level is high because the July 24, 2026 Left students' rally from Sealdah to Dharmatala turned violent, with police using batons and tear gas to disperse crowds after shoes were hurled and stones pelted, resulting in injuries and arrests. The merger of the CJP group, which lacked police clearance, with the Left-led march at Dharmatala escalated tensions and led to clashes between police and protesters. The convergence of multiple large crowds in central Kolkata, including the CJP rally and other student agitations, created a volatile environment. Police adopted a strict posture with barricades and force deployment, and the situation remains tense with potential for further escalation. No confirmed reports of mass detentions or Section 144/163 imposition are available, but the use of force and injuries justify a high danger level.
protests.status: The Left students' rally from Sealdah to Dharmatala (Esplanade) in central Kolkata took place on Friday, July 24, 2026, with thousands of students and youth affiliated with Left parties and their student wings, including the SFI, marching in solidarity with Delhi students who faced police action during the 'Sansad Chalo' march. The rally demanded justice for injured students, the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, and the scrapping of the NTA over exam irregularities. Police stated that a group claiming to support the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), which had been denied police clearance for its own rally, merged with the Left-led march at Dharmatala, significantly swelling the crowd. The protest turned violent, with police using batons and tear gas to disperse crowds after shoes were hurled and stones pelted, resulting in injuries and arrests. Visuals from the scene showed a massive crowd near Sealdah Station and along the route, and a road blockade was reported. The situation remains tense, and further protests are expected.
details: Police presence: Kolkata Police deployed barricades and forces at Esplanade and along the Sealdah–Dharmatala route; batons and tear gas were used to disperse crowds on July 24, 2026. Police denied permission for the CJP and Left student rallies citing Ulto Rath processions, but the march proceeded and was met with force.

Recent incidents: On July 24, 2026, the SFI-led rally turned violent at Esplanade after shoes were hurled and stones pelted; police used batons and tear gas, leaving several injured and some arrested. A road blockade was reported, and unidentified elements were blamed for hijacking the march.
Medical access: No specific information on hospitals, ambulances, or medical access is available in the search results. Injuries were reported but details on medical response are lacking.
Legal support: No information on legal aid organizations, helplines, or court interventions is available in the search results. Arrests occurred, but legal status of detainees is unknown.

protests.location: Multiple locations across Kolkata including state secretariat area, major road intersections, and railway tracks near Sealdah and Howrah stations
protests.cause: Protesting against alleged non-payment and severe delays in disbursement of Annapurna Yojana food security benefits to elderly beneficiaries across West Bengal, demanding immediate release of pending funds and accountability from the state food and supplies department.
protests.dangerReason: The danger level remains high due to active disruption of public infrastructure, including road and railway blockades by protesting women across multiple districts in West Bengal, as reported within the last 1-3 days. Protesters have stormed Seva Setu camps and allegedly damaged camp property, indicating a heightened risk of confrontations with authorities. The involvement of a Block Development Officer's alleged objectionable remarks in Malda district adds a volatile dimension. While no police violence or mass detentions are explicitly reported, the pattern of targeting government camps and blocking critical transport routes poses significant safety and legal risks. The state's acknowledgment of 1.58 crore transfers for September, alongside unresolved Aadhaar-bank linkage issues, suggests the agitation may persist.
protests.status: Protests over delayed and non-payment of Annapurna Yojana food security benefits continue across West Bengal, with women beneficiaries blocking roads, railway tracks, and disrupting government offices in Kolkata and other districts. The agitation has spread to multiple locations, including near Sealdah and Howrah stations, where railway tracks were blocked, and confrontations with political leaders have occurred. In Harishchandrapur, Malda district, women blocked roads after a Block Development Officer allegedly made objectionable remarks. The state government claims it has processed 1.58 crore transfers for September, but beneficiaries say they have not received the promised Rs 3,000 monthly assistance. Opposition leaders have blamed each other for the delays, with Mamata Banerjee accusing the BJP of breaking promises and BJP leaders citing system problems and sabotage. The protests show no signs of abating, with beneficiaries demanding immediate release of pending funds and accountability from the state food and supplies department.

protests.name: Jadavpur University FETSU Clash and Student Protest
protests.location: Gate 4 of Jadavpur University, Raja Subodh Chandra Mallick Road, Jadavpur, South Kolkata
protests.cause: Protesting against the forced cancellation of the FETSU (Faculty of Engineering and Technology Students' Union) meeting and alleged police brutality against students, with ABVP and Left-affiliated students demanding the right to hold democratic student union meetings without administrative or police interference.
protests.dangerReason: Multiple independent reports confirm actual physical violence between rival student groups at Jadavpur University on 19-20 August 2026, not merely tension: ABVP and Left-leaning (SFI/DSF) students clashed during a FETSU general body meeting, with several students from both camps injured and hospitalised at KPC Medical College Hospital. Reports describe stone-pelting, arson, vandalism, torn posters, and flags being set on fire, with clashes spilling onto the streets near Gate 4 where ABVP protesters breached barricades and clashed with police. A complaint naming 11 people was filed, and both blocs accused each other of bringing outsiders onto campus, raising the risk of renewed confrontation. The university has been closed indefinitely and the Vice Chancellor was hospitalised after falling ill during a meeting on the unrest, underscoring the severity. With rival groups planning further demonstrations and a probe committee only now beginning its work, the potential for fresh violence remains high.
protests.status: Jadavpur University in South Kolkata remains tense after a violent clash between ABVP and Left-leaning (SFI/DSF) student groups that erupted late on 19 August 2026 during a FETSU general body meeting near Gate 4 on Raja Subodh Chandra Mallick Road, continuing past midnight into 20 August. Several students from both camps were injured and admitted to KPC Medical College Hospital, with reports of stone-pelting, arson, vandalism, torn posters, and flags set on fire; both sides accused each other of bringing outsiders onto campus. Fresh clashes spilled onto the streets on 20 August as ABVP protesters breached barricades at Gate 4 and clashed with police, and the BJP publicly distanced itself from the RSS-backed student body. Police were deployed outside the university after authorities sought assistance, and additional security forces remained around the campus amid fears of further clashes. A complaint naming 11 people was filed, and rival student organisations planned demonstrations around the university and the 8B Bus Stand. A probe committee constituted by the university is scheduled to hold its first meeting this week after the Vice Chancellor, who had fallen ill during a meeting on the unrest, rejoined. No negotiated settlement or formal conclusion of the FETSU dispute has been announced.

protests.name: Anti-'Cockroach' Movement Solidarity Protest in Kolkata
protests.location: Dharmatala–Esplanade area, central Kolkata
protests.cause: Protesters are demonstrating in solidarity with the nationwide 'Cockroach' movement, which emerged as a backlash against the BJP's alleged media narrative control and the broader crackdown on student protesters following the CJP rallies. The movement critiques the Modi government's politics of suppression and demands protection of democratic dissent.
protests.dangerReason: The danger level remains high because of confirmed police violence at the July 24, 2026 Esplanade rally in Kolkata, where police blocked a CJP-Left students' march from Sealdah and deployed tear gas, leaving several people injured. The West Bengal government has invoked the Goonda Act against 14 arrested protesters, 13 of whom are Muslim, and the Chief Minister has used communal labels ('Friday people', 'Jamatis', 'Islamists') to justify the crackdown, indicating a hostile and communalized state posture. Nationwide, the crackdown is ongoing and politically charged: Mamata Banerjee and TMC MPs were detained for nearly four hours in Delhi on October 11-12, 2026, and reports document FIRs, lathi charges and water cannons against protesters across states. The movement continues to expand despite these measures, with CJP leaders vowing further election-related protests, keeping the potential for renewed clashes in Kolkata elevated. No new Kolkata-specific incident has been confirmed since July 24, 2026, so the assessment reflects a tense, unresolved standoff rather than active ongoing violence in the city.

Nationally, the movement continues to expand: the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has called for nationwide protests, and over a 48-hour period student-led protests engulfed almost every state despite FIRs, lathi charges and water cannons. On October 11-12, 2026, former CM Mamata Banerjee and TMC MPs were detained for nearly four hours in Delhi, and 'cockroach' movement leaders have publicly vowed to keep up election-related protests. West Bengal's government has invoked the Goonda Act against 14 arrested protesters, including 13 Muslims, while the Chief Minister has used communal rhetoric ('Friday people', 'Jamatis', 'Islamists') to characterize demonstrators. Organizers plan further nationwide actions, but no specific new Kolkata date or venue has been confirmed in the latest reports.

protests.location: Jadavpur and Gariahat areas, South Kolkata
protests.cause: Women protesters are organizing against the 'ugly pushback' they faced after participating in CJP protests, including online harassment, physical intimidation, and gendered abuse. The protest demands accountability for threats against women demonstrators and an end to the culture of intimidation targeting female activists.
protests.dangerReason: The danger level remains high due to the gendered nature of the threats and the volatile context of the Jadavpur University area, which has recently seen violent clashes between ABVP and Left students, including barricades breached at Gate 4 and police use of force. The protest's proximity to this campus increases the risk of targeted violence against women demonstrators. Although no new incidents have been reported in the current search intelligence, the previous assessment noted that one woman was followed near Gariahat on August 2, and participants have received threatening messages. Police response has been reactive rather than protective, with no dedicated security for women protesters, leaving them vulnerable. The broader national context of pushback against women after CJP protests, including doxxing and physical intimidation in Delhi, Mumbai, and Kolkata, further elevates the risk.
protests.status: The Women's Safety Pushback Protest in Jadavpur and Gariahat areas of South Kolkata continues as a small, localized demonstration by approximately 100-150 women, primarily students and activists. The protest began in early August 2025 and has maintained a presence near Jadavpur University Gate 4 and Gariahat crossing. Kolkata Police have deployed roughly 50-70 personnel with barricades at these locations, but no dedicated women's safety units have been assigned. Organizers report that several participants have received threatening messages, and one woman was followed near Gariahat on August 2. The protesters plan to submit a memorandum to the Kolkata Police Commissioner and hold a sit-in at Jadavpur 8B bus stand if their demands are not met within a week. No new incidents of violence or mass detentions have been reported in the current search intelligence, which largely covers broader CJP protest fallout and unrelated student protests. The situation remains tense but has not escalated further in the past week.

protests.name: Anti-Encroachment and Illegal Buildings Protest
protests.location: Residential and commercial neighborhoods across Bhopal affected by encroachments and illegal construction
protests.cause: Local residents are taking to the streets against encroachments and illegal buildings in their neighborhoods, demanding that authorities take action against unauthorized construction and restore public spaces. The protest reflects frustration over perceived inaction by municipal authorities.
protests.dangerReason: The danger level remains high due to recent incidents of self-immolation and clashes with police. A street vendor attempted self-immolation during a BMC encroachment drive at 10 Number Market, indicating extreme desperation. Additionally, traders clashed with police, broke barricades, and disrupted traffic during a protest march from New Market towards CM House. These events, combined with ongoing demolitions and the threat of an indefinite strike, elevate the risk of further escalation and violence. The recent relocation of 35 families from Deepak Nagar slum to Bag Mugalia adds to the tension, as residents protest the move.
protests.status: Residents and traders in Bhopal continue to hold rival marches over land-use demands as a Supreme Court deadline looms. Traders are demanding a mixed-use policy and a new master plan to protect businesses, while residents are urging action on illegal constructions. The Bhopal Municipal Corporation (BMC) has continued its anti-encroachment drives, including demolishing 63 illegal structures near the Upper Lake and clearing encroachments across the city. The Madhya Pradesh High Court took note of two women detained en route after habeas corpus petitions were filed, and the Additional Advocate General issued an urgent communication to senior police officials. Train services are scheduled to return to normal on October 11, but traveller associations continue to demand special trains or alternative arrangements.

protests.dangerReason: This is a large-scale, multi-district mobilisation ('Chalo Hyderabad') explicitly modelled on earlier student marches that drew heavy police deployment and barricading in Hyderabad. Polytechnic students have already staged a prior 'Chalo Hyderabad' march against the same SHAKTI/Young India Skill University merger, indicating a repeat confrontation with police at Dharna Chowk and Indira Park, where Section 144-style restrictions and barricades are routinely imposed. Mass detention of marching students, road closures on major arteries, and possible lathi-charge or water-cannon use at choke points near the Assembly are realistic risks given the state's firm posture against student agitation.
protests.status: Government polytechnic students across Telangana have announced a fresh 'Chalo Hyderabad' march for August 22, 2026, escalating their campaign against the merger of polytechnic colleges into Young India Skill University. Organisers say contingents from district polytechnic campuses will converge on Hyderabad, with the main body gathering at Dharna Chowk and Indira Park before attempting to march toward the Assembly and Higher Education offices. This follows an earlier Polytechnic 'Chalo Hyderabad' march against the SHAKTI Department merger, which was met with police barricading and detentions. Student unions are coordinating through campus committees and social media, and have appealed for a peaceful, disciplined march. Police have not yet issued formal permission, and Hyderabad and Cyberabad police are expected to deploy large numbers at entry points to the city and around the Assembly. Students plan to submit a memorandum to the Higher Education Minister and threaten an indefinite sit-in if demands are not met.
details: Police presence: Heavy deployment expected at Dharna Chowk, Indira Park, Tank Bund, and Assembly approach roads; barricades, RSI (Rapid Action Force) units, drones and possible water cannons; city entry points from NH-44 and NH-65 likely to be picketed.

Legal support: Student unions and civil-liberties lawyers associated with the Telangana Vidyarthi Vedika and similar groups are expected to provide legal aid; no dedicated helpline announced yet. Detained students in past marches were released on personal bond after station-level processing.

protests.name: DMK Thanjavur Cauvery Water Rights Protest
protests.location: Thanjavur district (Delta region), with solidarity demonstrations expected in Chennai at DMK headquarters, Anna Salai
protests.cause: DMK is protesting against what it calls TVK's betrayal of farmers and demanding firm steps to protect Tamil Nadu's Cauvery water rights, along with a special relief package for delta farmers affected by water shortages.
protests.dangerReason: The situation escalated beyond the prior assessment: Udhayanidhi Stalin was arrested by a joint Thanjavur-Neelankarai police team despite a Madras High Court oral order that no action be taken until a noon hearing, and he was taken on a roughly 300-km transit for questioning. DMK workers protested the detention across parts of Tamil Nadu, including Chennai, and a Pudukkottai MLA was among those detained, indicating multiple arrests and a tense standoff between police and party cadres. There are no confirmed reports of lathi charges, tear gas, or protester injuries, so the level is high rather than critical, but the arrest of a senior opposition leader and the resulting statewide protests carry clear potential for further escalation. The controversy over Udhayanidhi's remark has added a volatile political dimension, drawing sharp criticism online and from rival parties, which could inflame tensions further.
protests.status: The DMK staged its announced Cauvery water rights demonstration in Thanjavur on August 3, 2026, with Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin leading the protest and criticising the TVK-led government as 'incompetent' over the Cauvery issue and farmers' plight. The demonstration demanded firm steps to protect Tamil Nadu's Cauvery water rights and a special relief package for delta farmers, and coincided with Chief Minister Vijay's proposed Karnataka visit over the Mekedatu dam row. During the event, Udhayanidhi made a remark after supporters chanted a film actress's name, triggering a political and online controversy; DMK spokesperson TKS Elangovan later defended him, saying people were twisting his speech. Udhayanidhi was subsequently detained for questioning by a joint team of Thanjavur and Neelankarai police, and reports state the Madras High Court had orally ordered no action until a noon hearing, yet police arrested him by 11 a.m. and took him on a roughly 300-km transit for probe. Protests erupted in parts of Tamil Nadu, including Chennai, after the detention, with a Pudukkottai MLA among those detained; the DMK alleged the arrest was aimed at preventing him from raising the Cauvery issue in the Legislative Assembly. DMK chief M.K. Stalin has separately urged Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay to convene an all-party meeting on the Cauvery dispute.

protests.location: Outside Cockroach Janta Party founder's residence/office, Ahmedabad
protests.cause: Two youths from Ahmedabad are demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner over alleged irregularities in the voter list. They are protesting under the banner of the Cockroach Janta Party and have initiated an indefinite hunger strike.
protests.dangerReason: The situation remains critical due to mass detentions and heavy police crackdown. Over 70 protesters were detained in Ahmedabad, including women, journalists, and seniors, and activists allege further detentions. In Delhi, chaos erupted as protesters tried to reach Jantar Mantar, and high-profile leaders like Neha Bora were detained. The active enforcement of restrictions and widespread detentions indicate a severe crackdown with a high risk of further escalation and potential violence. Although a court released some leaders on October 11, 2026, the protest continues and police posture remains aggressive.

protests.name: Sansad Chalo Protest — 150 Detained in Ahmedabad
protests.location: Ahmedabad citywide, with detentions reported near major thoroughfares and government buildings; protesters attempted to march toward parliamentary-linked offices
protests.cause: Protesters demanded action on alleged exam paper leaks and broader education irregularities, including the NEET-UG paper leak scandal, and called for accountability from central education authorities. The 'Sansad Chalo' (March to Parliament) call was issued by the Cockroach Janta Party movement.
protests.dangerReason: Ahmedabad police detained approximately 150 protesters during the Sansad Chalo march, a mass detention event indicating a heavy-handed police response to a peaceful demonstration. All detainees were later released, but the scale of preemptive detention signals authorities are treating the movement as a security concern. The protest is linked to the broader Cockroach Janta Party movement, which has become the biggest youth challenge to PM Narendra Modi since 2014, raising the risk of escalation at future gatherings.
protests.status: On the day of the Sansad Chalo call, Ahmedabad police detained around 150 protesters over alleged paper leaks and education irregularities before releasing them all. The protesters had gathered to march in support of the national Cockroach Janta Party movement, which originated as social media satire and has grown into a Gen Z-led campaign against corruption and youth unemployment. Police adopted a preventive detention posture rather than allowing the march to proceed, mirroring crackdowns in other cities. The Cockroach Janta Party leadership has said a federal minister promised talks on their demands, suggesting the movement may shift toward negotiations. Protesters in Ahmedabad are expected to regroup and continue localized actions tied to the national campaign.
details: Police presence: Heavy deployment across Ahmedabad with preventive detention teams; approximately 150 protesters picked up, likely using vans and temporary holding points rather than static barricades.
Recent incidents: Around 150 Sansad Chalo protesters detained in Ahmedabad over paper leak and education irregularity demands; all were later released without reported injuries.

The involvement of right-wing groups and communal undertones, including demands to 'prove you're not Muslim', indicate a high risk of further clashes. The school's decision to make the books optional and the DEO's directive to sack a consultant show ongoing institutional pressure, which could fuel further protests and counter-protests.
